transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Poor drying on Bosch condenser dryers is most often caused by restricted airflow rather than a broken part. The two most common culprits are a blocked lint filter or a clogged condenser unit (the white plastic block at the bottom front), which prevents moist air from escaping. 1. Lint Filter: Open the door and remove the filter at the bottom of the door opening. Is it full of fluff?
2. Condenser: Open the small flap at the bottom left of the front panel. Also, were the clothes very wet when you put them in? If they weren't spun well in the washing machine (e.g.Please let me know if the filters were clogged and how wet the laundry was.
Door filter has fluff and a waxy film, rinsed it under the tap and water barely passes through until I scrubbed it. Haven't looked at the condenser yet. Clothes were a normal load, 1200 spin.

That waxy film on your lint filter is a classic sign that the condenser needs cleaning too; if air can't pass through the condenser, moisture stays in the drum. Please open the small flap at the bottom left of the front panel and remove the white plastic condenser block. Is it clogged with fluff or debris, and have you rinsed it clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
Never cleaned it before. Took it out and the front face is matted with lint. Rinsed it with the shower head and it's come clean. Anything else to do before I put it back?

Yes, let the condenser unit drip-dry completely before putting it back in; if you reinsert it while wet, it can cause mould or odours. Once it's dry, slide it back into its housing at the bottom of the door and close the flap securely. This blockage was probably why your clothes were coming out damp—without clear airflow, the moisture couldn't escape. It is worth cleaning both the lint filter and this condenser unit every few cycles to keep it running efficiently. Let me know if you need anything else!
